label: Duistermaat-Heckman Theorems
notes: This closing lecture spans printed pages 189 through 196. We push the Liouville volume forward along a torus moment map and discover that the resulting density is piecewise polynomial. The two Duistermaat-Heckman theorems package that fact, and the circle case proof drives every claim we make today.

label: Liouville and Pushforward
notes: Start from the Liouville measure built from omega to the n over n factorial, the canonical symplectic volume. Pushing it forward by a proper moment map gives the Duistermaat-Heckman measure on the dual Lie algebra. Its Radon-Nikodym density against Lebesgue is the object whose regularity the whole lecture explains.

label: The Sphere Example
notes: The sphere with height moment map is the cleanest illustration. A horizontal band over an interval has area exactly two pi times the height difference, independent of latitude. So the pushforward density is the constant two pi on the interval from minus one to one, our first explicit Duistermaat-Heckman measure.

label: DH Measure on the Polytope
notes: In general the density is constant on each chamber of regular values but jumps or bends at critical values, where the topology of the level set changes. The graph is polynomial on each chamber and only piecewise polynomial across breaks. That qualitative shape is the heart of the first Duistermaat-Heckman theorem.

label: Local Form for Reductions
notes: For a circle action the proof builds a local model near a regular level. A tubular neighborhood looks like Z times an interval, and we write sigma as pi star omega-red minus d of x alpha, with alpha a connection. This single normal form controls every reduced space in the interval at once.

label: Nondegeneracy and Projection
notes: At x equal to zero the form sigma reduces to the reduced symplectic form plus alpha wedge dx, which is nondegenerate, so it stays symplectic for small x. The same form gives i of X applied to sigma equal to dx, so the projection x is itself the moment map. The level x equals t reduces to the same quotient.

label: Linear Variation of the Class
notes: Reducing at level t yields omega-red minus t beta, where beta is the curvature of the connection and represents the Chern class of the circle bundle. Hence the reduced cohomology class varies affinely: it is the class at c-zero plus c minus c-zero times the fixed Euler class. This is the second Duistermaat-Heckman theorem.

label: Polynomial Volume
notes: Take the top power of the affine class to get the symplectic volume of the reduced space. Expanding omega-red minus t beta to the n minus one over factorial gives a polynomial in t of degree at most n minus one. By a Fubini computation this reduced volume equals the Duistermaat-Heckman density near the regular level.

label: Toric Constant Density
notes: On a toric manifold the density is the constant two pi to the n on the whole moment polytope. So the symplectic volume of the manifold is two pi to the n times the Euclidean volume of the polytope. The sphere example is exactly this statement in dimension two, with the segment as polytope.

label: Equivariant Cohomology Bridge
notes: Homework twenty-three frames everything through the Cartan model. The differential d minus i of X times x squares to zero on invariant forms, and omega plus mu x is equivariantly closed precisely when mu is a moment map. Localization then computes such integrals from fixed point data, explaining the stationary phase connection.

label: Synthesis
notes: To close the course: moment maps cannot scatter symplectic volume arbitrarily. On regular chambers the pushforward density is polynomial because reduced symplectic classes move affinely and their top powers are polynomial. Toric manifolds are the constant-density extreme, and equivariant localization gives the exact stationary phase formula underneath it all.
